sources.title: Yang-Mills & the Mass Gap
sources.scope: Current institutional problem status and overview.
sources.claim_boundary: The problem remains unsolved; the page is not a theorem source for partial results.

sources.title: Quantum Yang-Mills Theory
sources.scope: Canonical four-dimensional existence and physical mass-gap target, axiomatic floor, observable and ultraviolet requirements.
sources.claim_boundary: Defines the target and consequences; does not supply a construction or gap proof.

sources.title: Gauge field theories on a lattice
sources.scope: Reflection positivity and positive transfer matrix for lattice approximations; strong-coupling infinite-volume analyticity and Wilson confinement bound.
sources.claim_boundary: Fixed-lattice and strong-coupling results do not establish the asymptotically free four-dimensional continuum theory.

sources.title: Ultraviolet stability of three-dimensional lattice pure gauge field theories
sources.scope: Ultraviolet stability for three-dimensional lattice pure gauge theories.
sources.claim_boundary: Three-dimensional ultraviolet stability is not four-dimensional existence or a physical mass gap.

sources.title: Renormalization group approach to lattice gauge field theories I: generation of effective actions in a small field approximation and a coupling constant renormalization in four dimensions
sources.scope: Four-dimensional small-field renormalization-group construction of localized effective actions and coupling renormalization.
sources.claim_boundary: The small-field approximation and RG control are not a complete continuum measure, OS reconstruction, or mass-gap theorem.

sources.title: YM2: continuum expectations, lattice convergence, and lassos
sources.scope: Two-dimensional continuum Yang-Mills expectations, Wilson-lattice convergence, and measurable lasso variables.
sources.claim_boundary: Two-dimensional constructive control does not transfer to the four-dimensional target without a theorem.

sources.title: Yang-Mills measure on compact surfaces
sources.scope: Rigorous Yang-Mills measure on compact two-dimensional surfaces.
sources.claim_boundary: Compact-surface Euclidean measure is not the four-dimensional Minkowski theory.

sources.title: Langevin dynamic for the 2D Yang-Mills measure
sources.scope: Distributional connections, gauge-orbit state space, and gauge-covariant stochastic Yang-Mills heat flow in two dimensions.
sources.claim_boundary: Two-dimensional stochastic quantization does not construct the four-dimensional theory.

sources.title: A State Space for 3D Euclidean Yang-Mills Theories
sources.scope: A state-space framework for three-dimensional Euclidean Yang-Mills on the unit torus under a GFF-like regularity assumption.
sources.claim_boundary: The paper is conditional on the stated short-distance behaviour and does not construct a four-dimensional continuum theory or mass gap.

sources.title: Stochastic quantisation of Yang-Mills-Higgs in 3D
sources.scope: Local-in-time renormalized stochastic Yang-Mills-Higgs flow and gauge-covariant Markov process on gauge orbits, up to possible finite-time blow-up.
sources.claim_boundary: Three-dimensional Yang-Mills-Higgs local dynamics is not pure four-dimensional Yang-Mills existence or a mass-gap proof.

sources.title: A Stochastic Analysis Approach to Lattice Yang-Mills at Strong Coupling
sources.scope: Infinite-volume strong-coupling lattice Yang-Mills for SU(N) and SO(N), with functional inequalities, exponential correlation decay, and a lattice mass gap under explicit coupling bounds.
sources.claim_boundary: The result is at fixed lattice regulator and strong coupling; it does not survive the continuum limit by assertion.

sources.title: Rigorous solution of strongly coupled SO(N) lattice gauge theory in the large N limit
sources.scope: Strong-coupling large-N Wilson-loop expectations for SO(N) lattice gauge theory in any dimension.
sources.claim_boundary: Large N, strong coupling, and lattice observables do not establish finite-N four-dimensional continuum Yang-Mills.

sources.title: Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories
sources.scope: Perturbative asymptotic freedom of non-Abelian gauge theory.
sources.claim_boundary: Perturbative beta-function control is not a nonperturbative construction or mass-gap theorem.

sources.title: Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?
sources.scope: Independent perturbative demonstration of asymptotic freedom.
sources.claim_boundary: Perturbative asymptotic freedom does not establish the full nonperturbative theory.

sources.title: Axioms for Euclidean Green's Functions
sources.scope: Euclidean axioms and reconstruction route.
sources.claim_boundary: The reconstruction theorem applies only after every required axiom and regularity hypothesis is proved.

sources.title: Axioms for Euclidean Green's Functions II
sources.scope: Corrected and completed Euclidean reconstruction conditions.
sources.claim_boundary: Reflection positivity alone is not the complete OS profile.

sources.title: The four-dimensional Yang-Mills partition function in the vicinity of the vacuum
sources.scope: A proposed treatment of a four-dimensional partition function near the vacuum.
sources.claim_boundary: A partition-function result near a selected regime is not accepted here as the complete local-field construction or mass-gap theorem.

sources.title: A Constructive Proof of Existence and Mass Gap for Pure SU(3) Yang-Mills in Four-Dimensional Space-Time
sources.scope: Claims a complete SU(3) construction and mass gap.
sources.claim_boundary: Not independently audited or accepted by the governing Clay status; SU(3) alone would also not discharge universal compact-simple quantification.

sources.title: Reflection-Positive Construction of a Four-Dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills Theory with Mass Gap and Confinement
sources.scope: Claims a reflection-positive continuum construction, gap, confinement, and universality for SU(N).
sources.claim_boundary: The claim requires independent line-by-line audit; it does not alter the governing open status.

sources.title: On Charge Conjugation, Correlations, Elitzur's Theorem and the Mass Gap Problem in Lattice SU(N) Yang-Mills Models in d=4 Dimensions
sources.scope: Fixed-lattice Hilbert-space sectors, correlators, Elitzur-type statements, and proposed implications for the lattice mass-gap problem.
sources.claim_boundary: The source concerns a regulated lattice model and does not claim a completed continuum limit in the ledger.

sources.title: Yang-Mills measure on the two-dimensional torus as a random distribution
sources.scope: Two-dimensional torus Yang-Mills measure represented as a random distribution.
sources.claim_boundary: Two-dimensional measure construction is a solved analogue, not the four-dimensional target.
